== REPLICAS: Why do these pods exist?

[F1] CONTEXT  replica-floor  Deployment/checkout/api
    The workload sits at its HPA floor (minReplicas=3, replicas=3). HPA will not scale it lower, so its 3 pod(s) keep holding 1.5 CPU and 3.0Gi memory even when idle.
    What it means: These pods exist because of configuration, not load. Lowering the minimum (or scaling to zero off-hours) is what frees this capacity.
    Confidence: high
    Evidence:
      - Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c .metadata.ownerReferences (controller) = ReplicaSet/api-7d9f
      - ReplicaSet/checkout/api-7d9f .metadata.ownerReferences (controller) = Deployment/api
      - Deployment/checkout/api .spec.replicas = 3
      - HorizontalPodAutoscaler/checkout/api .spec.minReplicas = 3

== REQUESTS: How big is each pod?

[F2] WARNING  requests-above-vpa  Deployment/checkout/api
    Pods of this workload request more than VPA api recommends: 2 request(s) above its upper bound and 0 more than 25% above its target. The VPA is in mode Off, so it only recommends.
    What it means: Each pod reserves more than it is likely to use, so fewer pods fit on a node and nodes look full on paper.
    Confidence: high
    Evidence:
      - Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c .spec.containers[api].resources.requests.cpu = 500m
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/checkout/api .status.recommendation.containerRecommendations[api].upperBound.cpu = 300m
      - Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c .spec.containers[api].resources.requests.memory = 1Gi
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/checkout/api .status.recommendation.containerRecommendations[api].upperBound.memory = 768Mi
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/checkout/api .spec.updatePolicy.updateMode = Off
    Unknowns:
      - VPA recommends from recent usage; a workload with rare peaks may still need its headroom.

[F3] WARNING  vpa-not-applied  Deployment/checkout/api
    VPA api recommends different requests, but its update mode is Off, so nothing applies them.
    What it means: The right size is known but not applied.
    Confidence: high
    Evidence:
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/checkout/api .spec.updatePolicy.updateMode = Off
      - Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c .spec.containers[api].resources.requests.cpu = 500m
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/checkout/api .status.recommendation.containerRecommendations[api].target.cpu = 150m
      - Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c .spec.containers[api].resources.requests.memory = 1Gi
      - VerticalPodAutoscaler/checkout/api .status.recommendation.containerRecommendations[api].target.memory = 512Mi

== POLICY: Where may they run, and may they move?

[F4] BLOCKER  no-room-elsewhere  Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c
    None of the 3 other schedulable node(s) in the snapshot can take this pod. Draining this node would leave it Pending, so autoscalers keep the node.
    What it means: The other nodes say no because of: pod anti-affinity on 2 node(s), taint on 1 node(s).
    Applies to: cluster-autoscaler, karpenter
    Confidence: medium
    Evidence:
      - Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c requests (containers, init containers, overhead) = cpu=500m memory=1Gi
      - Node/general-a fit check = pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname: Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-a already runs there
      - Node/general-b fit check = pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname: Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-b already runs there
      - Node/ml-a fit check = taint dedicated=ml:NoSchedule not tolerated
    Other explanations:
      - Karpenter may replace this node with a cheaper one instead of deleting it; this rule only checks moving pods onto existing nodes.
      - Requests may be larger than real usage; right-sizing (for example with VPA recommendations) could create room.
    Unknowns:
      - Placement is a first-fit estimate by requests, largest pod first; a different packing might succeed.
      - Volume zones, pod priority and preemption were not evaluated.

== NODES: Will the node autoscaler remove or replace the node?

[F5] CONTEXT  karpenter-not-consolidatable-yet  Node/general-c
    Karpenter has not marked this node consolidatable yet, so it does not consider removing or replacing it. NodePool general waits consolidateAfter (1m) after pods were last added to or removed from a node.
    Applies to: karpenter
    Confidence: medium
    Evidence:
      - NodeClaim/general-c-x3 .status.conditions[Consolidatable].status = False (at 2026-11-21T02:59:30Z)
      - NodePool/general .spec.disruption.consolidateAfter = 1m
    Unknowns:
      - Frequent pod churn on the node keeps restarting this wait.

Limitations:
  - Snapshot heuristic, not a scheduler simulation: placement checks cover node selectors, required node affinity, taints, required pod (anti-)affinity, topology spread and host ports, but not volume zones, priorities, preemption or preferred rules.
  - Autoscaler settings are read where the cluster exposes them (Karpenter NodePools and NodeClaims), not Cluster Autoscaler flags or node group minimums.
  - One point in time: PDB status, replica counts and events change.
  - Packing is measured with resource requests, not real usage.
  - Pod size is judged only where a VPA recommendation exists; other workloads are unknowns.
  - Read-only: KubeShrink never modifies a cluster.
